#ETH  Do you think you can make a profit in the crypto space just by relying on skills, news, or inspiration? If that's your mindset, you’re being naive and just destined to be a noob. The only people who can survive in this market and turn their fortunes around are those who have been ground into the dirt by the market, have lost so much they felt like jumping off a building, yet still grit their teeth and get back up.
Here’s my experience over the past 10 years—it's blunt but not lacking in logic (I suggest giving it a like and saving it so you can find it later).
1. If you’ve never been liquidated, you’ll always be a rookie. 
If you’ve never felt the pain of a liquidation, you don’t truly understand what “pain” means. 
If you’ve never gone from a profit of 100k to losing it all, you’ll never grasp the meaning of “despair.” 
The market doesn’t care about your feelings; it teaches you the hard way: 
If you lose 50% of 100k, you’re left with 50k, but to recover, you need to double that.
Climbing from the 1st floor to the 100th takes an hour, but jumping from the 100th floor only takes 30 seconds.
(Remember this): 
Your capital is crucial!! 
Even if you’ve doubled it 100 times, just one time hitting zero means you’re completely out.
2. Why are most people noobs? 
Because they can’t control themselves! 
They’ll spend 3 days comparing prices for a pair of shoes but decide on buying crypto in just 3 seconds! 
The pain of losing 1000 bucks is 10 times more intense than the joy of making 1000 bucks! 
Think ahead: 
In this market, how much do I want to gain? 
How much do I absolutely need to cut losses? 
How much do I need to withdraw after making a profit? 
Never go all-in: DCA (Dollar Cost Average) and always leave yourself a way out.
Be patient and wait for opportunities: The crypto world is a place where “three years of no action can lead to three years of gains”; moving recklessly equals disaster! 
3. Top-tier mindset: What you want isn’t just small profits; it’s a life-changing fortune! 
If you’re trading with 10k and losing sleep over a few hundred bucks in fluctuations, it’s best to exit now—you’re not cut out for this game! 
What do the real big players think? 
Their goal is 1 million, and they don’t even blink at a 10k fluctuation! 
When a trend comes, hold on tight; if there’s no trend, it’s better to sleep than to act recklessly! 
Trading goes against human nature; you need to be more patient than 99% of people. 
The market won’t eliminate those with poor skills; it will only eliminate those with a broken mindset. 
Do you want to be the noob who gets completely wiped out or the winner who can rise again after losing everything? The market waits for no one, and only those with ambition will be rewarded.

#ETH  Can you still make money in the crypto space?

Making some pocket change in crypto isn't too hard; it really depends on your capital. The simplest strategy is to watch the market daily, focusing mainly on BTC and Ethereum. Keep an eye on the trends for the past couple of weeks, and when the price dips to your target level, it's time to buy the dip. Wait until the price bounces back to a decent level and then sell off a few thousand – easy money!
When stepping into crypto, there are three things you should never do!
First, never buy when the price is climbing – be greedy when others are fearful and fearful when others are greedy. Make it a habit to buy when prices are down.
Second, never go all in.
Third, never have a full position; being fully invested makes you passive and in this market, opportunities are plentiful. The opportunity cost of being fully invested can be quite high.
Now, let's talk about the six short-term trading rules.
The first rule is that after the price consolidates at a high, it usually makes a new high. Conversely, after consolidating at a low, it often makes a new low. So, wait for clear signals before making moves.
The second rule is don't trade in sideways markets. Most traders lose money because they can't stick to this simple principle.
The third rule is when selecting candlesticks, buy on bearish closes and sell on bullish closes.
Fourth, when the downtrend slows, expect a weak rebound; if the downtrend accelerates, a strong rebound may follow.
Fifth, adopt a pyramid buying strategy for building your positions. This is the only constant in value investing.
Sixth, when a coin is on a sustained rise or fall, it will eventually enter a consolidation phase. At this point, you don't need to sell everything at the top or buy in fully at the bottom. After consolidation, a trend change is inevitable. If it starts to break down from a high, it's time to clear your position. Just remember to act swiftly!

#opg $OPG  While flipping through the architecture diagram of @OpenGradient , there was a design that left a lump in my throat. In our current understanding of Web3, a pure on-chain large model network is nothing more than buyers placing orders, miners taking jobs, and finally quality inspectors giving the stamp of approval. However, this project has stubbornly wedged in a role called 'Facilitator' in the middle. $ETH #ETH 

The official line presents it as a 'coordinating hub.' But upon closer inspection, this is quite intriguing. The so-called coordination is equivalent to holding all the cards. It knows exactly where the orders come from, how much OPG is consumed, at what time it entered the market, and which machine it ultimately landed on. In this closed loop, the ones running the hash power are just ruthless work machines, and the quality inspectors are merely checking tools; only this coordinator possesses a god-like view of the entire chain.

This made me realize a logical flaw overlooked by the market. Everywhere you hear about the democratization of computing power, but breaking down GPUs and algorithms and distributing them is not difficult at all; the real barrier lies in the 'task dispatch mechanism.' No matter how much hardware there is, there needs to be a brain to direct the flow. Whoever controls the distribution of tasks has their hand on the throat of the entire chain. This is akin to platform hegemony from the classical internet era; what big companies value most is not the data centers but the gateways to traffic.

In relation to OpenGradient, the Facilitator is by no means a dispensable accessory but rather the 'traffic director' controlling the whole game. It doesn’t run any lines of code itself, nor does it bear the dirty work of verification, yet it decisively dictates the flow of all data. A few mining rigs may go down in the network, but the business continues; however, once this central node is unplugged, the entire ecosystem comes to a standstill in an instant.

Therefore, I am now extremely skeptical of its proclaimed decentralization. Strip away the outer layer and you’ll find that while the hardware has indeed gone rural and quality checks have been decentralized, the core 'allocation power' has not been relinquished at all; it merely wears an invisibility cloak called Facilitator. If this logic holds water, then moving forward with AI-related projects, the focus must shift. No longer fixate on which machines are more powerful; the future core battle lies not in who hoards the most GPUs but in who truly holds the command over these GPUs.

对应到 OpenGradient 这里，Facilitator 绝非可有可无的零配件，而是掌控全局的“交通局长”。它自己一行代码不跑，不承担验算的脏活，却实打实地决定着所有数据的流转。网络里宕机几台运算矿机，业务照旧；可一旦这个中枢节点拔了网线，整个生态瞬间就会停摆。

#opg $OPG  has recently been dissecting the white paper of @OpenGradient , and the more I look at it, the more I find the component called Facilitator a bit suspicious. According to the conventional understanding of distributed AI networks, it’s just a simple three-step process: clients place their demands, the compute side runs the models, and the verification side confirms. Yet this project awkwardly inserted a 'Coordinator' in the middle.

Upon closer examination, this coordinating action actually holds significant power. Because it means it has an omniscient perspective: it knows who placed the order, who paid the OPG toll, where the task card is in the process, and which machine it ultimately gets assigned to—it has the complete picture. The underlying machines just crunch the numbers, the verifiers just stamp the approval, but only it is all-knowing and all-powerful. $ETH #ETH 

Following this line of thought, I suddenly realized a blind spot in the industry. Right now, various projects are hyping up the decentralization of compute power, but in reality, the hardest nut to crack for AI on-chain has never been about stacking GPUs; it’s about how to 'allocate tasks.' Distributing hardware and models worldwide is easy, but the work always needs a source to distribute from. Whoever holds the distribution power holds the information hub of the entire ecosystem. Reflecting on the old internet logic, the most profitable players have always been the ones who control the flow gate.

In the context of the OpenGradient system, the Facilitator is not just a trivial add-on; it’s the dispatch room of the entire highway. It doesn’t produce results itself, nor does it handle quality control, but it controls the flow of all data. Lose two compute machines, and the network remains unaffected; but if this coordinating hub gets jammed, the entire business line comes to a halt.

So I now hold reservations about whether it has truly achieved 'decentralization.' To put it bluntly, while hardware and verification have indeed been decentralized, the core command baton has not been handed over; it’s merely a change of disguise. If this logic holds true, then moving forward, when evaluating such projects, don’t just focus on who has the most GPUs. The future’s real ace will not be about who owns the most devices, but about who has the power to allocate tasks to those devices.

#opg $OPG  Recently had a casual chat with a big node runner, and he dropped a bombshell about Crypto+AI: "The outputs generated on-chain, I don’t even trust a punctuation mark, yet I still have to back it up." Flipping through the whitepaper of @OpenGradient , it clearly states to use CometBFT, with a 10-second block time. It’s like dozens of couriers watching a locked metal box being stored, everyone signs off saying "the box is in", but no one has pried it open to see if it’s filled with cash or mud.

In this unspoken agreement, the market price around $0.22 for $OPG  has become the purest driving force. Distributing transaction fees and node rewards isn’t about spending money to uncover the truth, but rather buying everyone’s ‘nonchalance’. Once they get paid, they just check the format and stamp it, avoiding any deep digging.

Don’t think this is some grand loophole; it’s precisely the bitter fruit that the current architecture has to swallow. If thousands of machines were to recalculate the large model, those profits wouldn’t even cover the electricity bill. To keep the network alive, the consensus mechanism can only concede, downgrading the relentless battle over 'content correctness' to a mere formality of 'process compliance'. What’s stored on the ledger is always just a receipt of 'calculations having occurred', rather than an 'absolute truth'.

这里必须提一下 $OPG 的特殊定位。它可不止是单纯拿来当Gas烧掉或者炒作价格那么简单，更像是个算力资源的调度枢纽。系统底层看这个资产信号下菜碟，自动决定任务走哪条通道、分配多大性能，甚至还能把跑完的数据反哺到下一次的分配机制里。这么一来，整个网络就像个有生命力的动态系统。

当然，没什么是绝对完美的。把运算和验证彻底拆解开，求稳确实没得说，但防范作恶的验证成本实在太高昂了。你要是搞高频套利这种要极速响应的活儿，这套框架肯定会拖后腿。所以，重构算力分发的协议确实是他们家的核心壁垒，但广大开发者最后愿不愿意为这种高昂的“可验证属性”掏真金白银买单，还得让子弹再飞一会儿看看。

Of course, the Achilles' heel of infrastructure projects is the long cycles. If the subsequent model library can’t keep up, the business will stagnate. This morning, while being pushed along at the subway transfer point, I suddenly thought of something. 

Some big funds entering the market are like someone dragging a suitcase against the crowd during the morning rush; they don’t make many moves, but you can’t help but glance back. 

This time, the new address withdrew 17,675 $ETH from Binance at a price of 1,617. The spot is now around 1,643, already showing a paper profit of 667,000 bucks. 

Honestly, the main point isn’t the tens of thousands in paper profit itself. 

The key is the subtlety of their positioning. 

$ETH 24 hours are actually still in a downtrend, about -1.3%, indicating that the surface sentiment isn’t that euphoric. 

But it hit a daily low of 1,552 and managed to bounce back to 1,643. This kind of retracement makes me feel like there’s someone buying below, not just a situation where it falls apart at the first touch. 

What concerns me more is that the contract volume is 17.7 times that of the spot. 

Watching this kind of market is exhausting; it shows many people aren’t gradually accumulating but are exhausting each other with leverage. 

The funding rate is only +0.0034%, and it hasn’t heated up absurdly, so I’m not inclined to interpret this withdrawal directly as a “high-point excitement relay.” 

It feels more like someone thinks it’s worth grabbing a bit of chips here, a decent cost-performance ratio. 

My trader friend once told me a pretty hard-hitting truth: The truly painful markets aren’t the ones that explode up or down; it’s when you clearly feel it’s weak, yet there are always buyers stepping in. 

Right now, $ETH  has a bit of that flavor. 

I personally lean a bit bullish, but not in that aggressive way of wanting to chase after it. 

If it can hold above this withdrawal cost of 1,617, I’d be more willing to see it as a strong signal. 

If it quickly drops back down, then this on-chain action is more like a pretty short-term trade point, not worth overthinking. 

I’m already worn out from charting during the day; at night, Doudou sits by the keyboard, staring at the screen, calmer than I am 😅 

In this section, I prefer to wait for a dip to reassess, not chasing highs, and I don’t want to get carried away emotionally in this leveraged market. 

The market can flip faster than you can turn a page, so I’ll keep some position. $ETH #ETH

content:
早上在地铁换乘口被人流推着走的时候，我突然想到一件事。

有些大资金进场，就像有人在早高峰里逆着人群拖行李箱，动作不多，但你就是会忍不住回头看一眼。

这次新地址从币安提了 17675 枚 $ETH，提出价格 1617，现在现货在 1643 附近，账面已经有 66.7 万刀浮盈。

讲真，重点不是这几十万浮盈本身。

重点是它挑的位置很微妙。

$ETH 24 小时其实还是跌的，-1.3% 左右，说明表面情绪没那么亢奋。

但它日内低点打到 1552，又能拉回 1643，这种回抽会让我觉得，下面有人在接，不是那种一碰就散的状态。

更让我有点在意的是，合约成交是现货的 17.7 倍。

这种盘看着就累，说明很多人不是在慢慢拿货，是在用杠杆互相耗。

资金费率只有 +0.0034%，又没热到离谱，所以我不太倾向把这次提币直接理解成“高位兴奋接力”。

更像是有人觉得，这里拿一点筹码，性价比还行。

我那个做 trader 的闺蜜以前跟我说过一句挺扎心的话：真正让人难受的盘，不是暴涨暴跌，是你明明觉得它弱，它却总有人接。

现在的 $ETH 就有点这个味道。

我个人偏多一点，但不是那种想追着开大的偏多。

如果后面还能稳在这次提币成本 1617 上面，我会更愿意把它当成一个偏强信号看。

要是很快又跌回去，那这笔链上动作更多就只是一次漂亮的短线卡点，不值得脑补太多。

我白天画图已经够累了，晚上回家豆豆蹲在键盘边上盯着屏幕，比我还冷静 😅

这一段我更倾向逢回踩再看，不追高，也不想在这种杠杆盘里情绪上头。

市场翻脸比翻书快，留点仓位。$ETH #ETH
